newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar futures end at five-month high.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar futures end at five-month high.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures settled at five-month highs on technically-driven fund buying and a dearth of selling in the March contract, market sources said.

The most-active May contract closed up 0.27 at 11.15, having ranged from 10.85 to 11.17, it highest level since reaching 11.24 cents September 24. Spot March settled 0.33 higher at 11.25. The contract rose to 11.30 also on September 24.
Volume was estimated at 56,212 lots compared with 34,674 lots Tuesday.
Light resistance was seen around 11.55 cents in March.

The widening of the March/May spread to 0.10 cent on the close compared with 0.04 Tuesday added to the perception of near-term tightness for delivery against March. The contract's last trading day is Friday, March 28.
One broker said the back months were under considerable pressure from selling at every point.
Refco analyst Anne Prendergast said talk that Brazil suspended a 500,000 tonne quota earlier today underpinned the technical move higher.

Brazil's said it would export 5.2 million tonnes of sugar with an additional 500,000 tonnes allowed to be freed for export. Widespread talk that the quota was suspended today because international prices are below domestic prices in Brazil, fueled bullish sentiment.
"People wanting to take delivery are worried that the sugar won't be there," Prendergast said.
